analysis:
The 2004-05 Budget speech proposed a 2 per cent cess on central taxes to fund universal elementary education. The accompanying Finance Ministry memorandum described it as an additional surcharge to finance the government's commitment to universalise quality basic education.

A subsequent Lok Sabha reply records that the education cess was levied at 2 per cent from 2004-05 and was used for basic education and the mid-day meal scheme; an additional 1 per cent cess for secondary and higher education followed in 2007-08.

The proposal was therefore implemented. The cess is an earmarked surcharge on taxes rather than a direct increase in the education budget.
